title: Rapid supercurrent decay in Mn$_5$Si$_3$ Josephson junctions
authors: Arjun Sapkota, Kurt Lorenzen, Tyler Kuhn, Juan Gomez, Demet Korucu, Robert M. Klaes, Reza Loloee, Norman O. Birge, Nathan Satchell
abstract: Theoretical work predicts that Josephson junctions containing metallic altermagnetic barriers should display $0$-$π$ transitions of the critical current as a function of both barrier thickness and temperature, with the decay and oscillation period of the supercurrent depending on the orientation of the crystal axes relative to the transport direction. Motivated by these predictions, and by reports of a compensated magnetic phase attributed to altermagnetism in epitaxial Mn$_5$Si$_3$ thin films, we fabricate and measure Nb/Pt/Mn$_5$Si$_3$/Pt/Nb Josephson junctions varying the thickness of the Mn$_5$Si$_3$ barrier. The critical current decays as a single exponential over more than four orders of magnitude with decay length $ξ_{\text{Mn}_5\text{Si}_3} = 0.31 \pm 0.03$ nm, shorter than reported for Josephson junctions containing the metallic antiferromagnets FeMn, Cr, and NiMn. The Mn$_5$Si$_3$ barrier has an estimated current-perpendicular-to-plane resistivity of $320 \pm 10 μΩ\,$cm. No $0$-$π$ transition is resolved at the sampled barrier thicknesses, and the temperature dependence of the critical current of a junction with a 1 nm barrier is smooth and monotonic. We discuss the absence of resolvable transitions in terms of the microstructure of the barrier, its uncertain magnetic phase, and the narrow thickness window imposed by the rapid decay, and identify barriers with well-defined crystalline orientation as the key requirement for future tests of altermagnetic Josephson physics.
summary: Researchers fabricated Josephson junctions using $	ext{Mn}_5	ext{Si}_3$ as a barrier to test predictions of $0-\pi$ transitions characteristic of metallic antiferromagnets. While the supercurrent decay was measured successfully, no oscillatory transitions were observed. The authors conclude that achieving clear signatures requires barriers with highly defined crystalline orientation.
main_problem: The study investigates supercurrent decay and the presence of predicted 0-$\pi$ transitions in Josephson junctions utilizing metallic altermagnetic barriers ($	ext{Mn}_5	ext{Si}_3$).
main_result: The critical current decays exponentially with a short length scale ($\xi = 0.31 \pm 0.03$ nm), and no oscillatory $0-\pi$ transitions were resolved, suggesting structural or magnetic disorder suppresses the predicted effects.
method: Electrical transport measurements (I-V characteristics) were performed on patterned $	ext{Nb}/	ext{Pt}/	ext{Mn}_5	ext{Si}_3/	ext{Pt}/	ext{Nb}$ junctions while varying barrier thickness and temperature.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Josephson junction where the superconducting barrier material is epitaxial $	ext{Mn}_5	ext{Si}_3$, an altermagnetic compound. Theoretical predictions suggested oscillatory behavior ($0-\pi$ transitions) dependent on crystal orientation.
key_observables: Critical current ($I_c$), supercurrent decay length ($\xi_{	ext{Mn}_5	ext{Si}_3}$), and the temperature dependence of $I_c$.
important_parameters: Supercurrent decay length $\xi_{	ext{Mn}_5	ext{Si}_3} = 0.31 \pm 0.03$ nm; Barrier resistivity $ho_{	ext{Mn}_5	ext{Si}_3} = 320 \pm 10 \, \mu\Omega	ext{cm}$.
main_assumptions: The absence of transitions is attributed to the microstructure, uncertain magnetic phase, and narrow thickness window, rather than a failure of the underlying theory.
figures_summary: Figures show $I_c R_N$ decay vs. thickness (single exponential fit) and $I_c R_N$ vs. Temperature (smooth/monotonic dependence). Structural characterization used XRR and XRD data.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical motivation for studying altermagnetic Josephson junctions, then details the fabrication and measurement of $	ext{Nb}/	ext{Pt}/	ext{Mn}_5	ext{Si}_3/	ext{Pt}/	ext{Nb}$ junctions. Results show exponential decay but lack oscillations, leading to a discussion on structural requirements for future tests.
why_interesting: This work directly probes the interplay between magnetism (altermagnetism) and superconductivity in nanoscale devices, which is highly relevant to superconducting quantum circuits and spintronics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic cross section of the Josephson junction device, with layer thicknesses given in (nm) as grown. The thickness of the Mn5Si3 layer ranges from 0.5 to 4.5 nm. (b,c) Product of the critical current and normal state resistance, IcRN, versus applied magnetic field for Josephson junctions with Mn5Si3 thicknesses of (b) 2.0 nm and (c) 1.0 nm at 4.2 K. The solid red lines are fits to the data of Eqs. 2 and 3. Inset of (b): the I–V characteristic of the same junction at zero applied field, together with the fit to Eq. 1 from which Ic and RN are determined.

FIG. 2. Thickness dependence of supercurrent in Mn5Si3 Josephson junctions. Top: Product of the critical current and normal state resistance, IcRN versus Mn5Si3 thickness at 4.2 K. The line is a best fit to Eq. 4 over the range 1–3.5 nm with decay length ξMn5Si3 = 0.31 ± 0.03 nm. Bottom: Area resistance product, ARN, for the junctions, where the best fit to Eq. 5 indicates the Mn5Si3 resistivity, ρ = 320±10 µΩcm. Each data point represents one Josephson junction and the uncertainty in determining IcRN and ARN is smaller than the data points.

FIG. 3. Product of the critical current and normal state resis- tance, IcRN versus temperature for a Josephson junction with Mn5Si3 thickness of 1.0 nm. The critical temperature is ap- proximately 8.8 K, and the trend of IcRN(T) is well described by the phenomenological expression, Eq. 6. Each data point represents IcRN extracted at one temperature and the uncer- tainty in determining IcRN is smaller than the data points.
